clue.text: Tory rebel worse off with Miliband, an uncomfortable diagnosis

indicators.note: something off has gone bad or wrong, so these letters are spoiled into a new order

explanation.surface: A political tale: a disaffected Conservative teaming up with the Labour leader Ed Miliband, which a doctor calls an awkward condition.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is all twenty-two letters of TORY REBEL WORSE plus MILIBAND; 'with' simply joins the two parts and 'an' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The condition is a medical finding that brings cramps and gut discomfort, so it is literally an unpleasant thing to be told by a doctor.

clue.text: A hunted-for key?

parts.note: piano keys were traditionally faced with elephant tusk material, for which elephants are poached

explanation.surface: Someone searching for a lost key.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'hunted-for key' sounds like one mislaid; it is a piano key made from the tusks that poachers hunt elephants for.
explanation.definitionFit: Old piano keys were covered in tusk material, a substance obtained by hunting elephants.

clue.text: Cameron's foreign affair

indicators.note: foreign means strange or alien, so the letters of the name are made unfamiliar by rearranging

parts.note: David Cameron was the Conservative Prime Minister; his surname gives the letters

explanation.surface: A tabloid story about David Cameron, then Prime Minister, having an affair abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: A love affair is a synonym for a romantic relationship, often a secret or brief one.

clue.text: Principle that can do a U-turn?

indicators.note: a word that can turn round and still be itself reads the same in both directions

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A jibe at politicians whose principles get abandoned in a policy U-turn.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenet is a belief or doctrine held as true, a synonym for a principle.

clue.text: Ex-minister covering commercial songs

indicators.note: covering means the name of the politician goes around the other piece

parts.note: Ed Balls was a Labour government minister until 2010
an ad is a commercial, an advertisement

explanation.surface: A former politician performing cover versions of jingles.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballads are narrative songs, often slow and sentimental, so the plural fits 'songs'.

clue.text: Parliamentary proposal written in detail, even parts provoking strong feeling

indicators.note: written in means the proposal is set inside the letters taken from the next word
the even parts are the second, fourth and sixth letters of the word detail

parts.note: a motion is a proposal put to Parliament for debate

explanation.surface: A detailed parliamentary motion whose passages stir up strong feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'even parts' means the even-numbered letters, not halves, and 'written in' makes the proposal a container's filling.
explanation.definitionFit: Something emotional stirs the passions, which is what provoking strong feeling describes.

clue.text: Twelve there, twelve back

parts.note: midday is twelve o'clock, and its word reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A clock reading twelve in one direction and twelve the other way round.
explanation.walkthrough: The word for midday reads the same backwards, so it is twelve going there and twelve coming back.
explanation.definitionFit: Midday is twelve o'clock, and the word is a palindrome, so it is twelve both ways.

clue.text: Old fart in reactionary, unjust

indicators.note: reactionary suggests a violent reaction, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Grumbling that an old fart among reactionaries is being treated unfairly.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unjust is unfair, the two-word phrase being a plain synonym.

clue.text: Standard Italian coastal region a non-starter up in Rome, perhaps?

indicators.note: in means the reversed region goes inside the rearranged city
perhaps suggests the city name might be rearranged differently
up in a down clue says the letters are read from bottom to top
a non-starter loses its start, so the opening letter a is removed

parts.note: the Amalfi Coast is a stretch of coastline in southern Italy

explanation.surface: A standard Italian coastline being taken north to Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a non-starter' takes the region's opening a away, 'up' turns the rest bottom to top, and it goes 'in' ORME, from Rome reworked ('perhaps'). Amalfi is the coastal region south of Naples.
explanation.definitionFit: The oriflamme was the sacred red banner of the French kings, hence any battle standard or flag.

clue.text: Ex-minister loves to replace articles with a line that's feeling moody?

indicators.note: the plural articles and loves mean the swap happens a second time, for the other article
replace says the articles in the name are swapped for the loves, one swap here

parts.note: Harriet Harman was a Labour government minister until 2010
a is the indefinite article; both of them in the name are swapped
love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter o

explanation.surface: A former minister in a mood about wording, swapping articles for a line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articles' and 'loves' are plural, so both letters a in the name become o; Harriet Harman was a Labour deputy leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Moodiness is often blamed on fluctuating glandular chemistry, so a person feeling moody may be called this.

clue.text: Get the better of the twerp from Balliol, say

parts.note: Balliol is a college of Oxford University, abbreviated OU
a twerp is a twit, a silly person

explanation.surface: Beating some silly Oxford student.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks Balliol as an example, not a sound-alike; Balliol is one of the colleges of Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: To outwit someone is to beat them by being cleverer, getting the better of them.

clue.text: Baby bird with canary, gyrfalcon and egret's wings

indicators.note: a bird's wings are on its two sides, so each word gives its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A young bird among a canary, a falcon and an egret, each spreading its wings.
explanation.definitionFit: A young swan is called a cygnet, so it is a specific kind of baby bird.

clue.text: Friendly minister not convinced by his own identity?

parts.words: not convinced by his own identity
parts.note: someone unsure who they are asks 'am I ...?'
Vince Cable was Business Secretary in the coalition government

explanation.surface: A minister wondering who he really is.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as the question 'Am I Cable?', asked by the Business Secretary Vince Cable doubting his own identity.
explanation.definitionFit: Amicable means good-natured and peaceable, a close synonym for friendly.

clue.text: On reflection, that is left, not right

indicators.note: not right means wrong, so the letters are put the wrong way round

explanation.surface: Thinking it over, that is on the left, not the right, like a mirror image.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that' is a link. The answer is a reflexive pronoun, the grammatical word for a self-reference, which is why 'On reflection' defines it.
explanation.definitionFit: Reflexive pronouns turn the action back on the subject, so the pun on reflection describes this grammatical self-reference word.

clue.text: Shape great among many quadrilaterals

indicators.note: among says the reworked letters sit inside the word for many

parts.note: tons means lots, a great many

indicators.note: to shape something is to mould it, so the letters of great are reformed

explanation.surface: Instructions to draw a great shape among lots of four-sided figures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shape' reworks GREAT as ETRAG, put 'among' TONS.
explanation.definitionFit: A tetragon is a polygon with four angles and four sides, so the plural means four-sided figures.

clue.text: Affairs involving great leader go up for punishment by the whips

indicators.note: involving means the affairs enclose the other letters

parts.note: flings are brief romantic affairs

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the letters are read from bottom to top
leader means the first letter of the word great

explanation.surface: A scandal: party whips punishing an MP for affairs with a party leader.
explanation.walkthrough: G from great's 'leader' plus GO turned 'up' gives OGG, placed in FLINGS. Whips are both party disciplinarians and lashes.
explanation.definitionFit: Beatings with a whip or cane are a form of corporal punishment administered with lashes.

clue.text: See 1
Valve hit, high-pitched note coming in

indicators.note: coming in means the note goes inside the word for hit

parts.note: to sock someone is to hit them
top C is a high note in singing

explanation.surface: A plumbing valve being struck as a shrill squeal comes out.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopcock is a tap or valve that controls the flow of water in a pipe.

clue.text: Raised up walls in behind a flat surface

indicators.note: walls in means the outer letters surround the rest like a wall
raised in a down clue says the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: behind means late, behind schedule

explanation.surface: Something raised up with walls built behind a flat area.
explanation.walkthrough: UP 'Raised' is PU, whose letters 'wall in' LATE and A.
explanation.definitionFit: A plateau is an area of high, level ground, so a raised flat surface.

clue.text: Where to find a crackpot like Mr Putin, ultimately?

definitions.text: Where to find a crackpot like Mr Putin, ultimately?

indicators.note: crackpot means crazy, so the letters go crazy and are rearranged
ultimately means at the end, picking the final letter of the name

explanation.surface: A dig at Vladimir Putin as a crank and where he can be found.
explanation.definitionFit: The Moscow citadel is the seat of the Russian presidency, where its president, Putin, works.

clue.text: Organ in song hoisted up

indicators.note: in means the newspaper sits inside the song

parts.note: a lied is a German art song
an organ is a newspaper; the Financial Times is FT

explanation.surface: An organ is lifted into place during a song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ' is a newspaper, not an instrument or body part.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lifted has been raised, the same as hoisted up.

clue.text: Two Tories in pursuit of the inedible

parts.note: Liam Fox was a Conservative defence secretary
Jeremy Hunt was a Conservative health secretary

explanation.surface: Two Conservatives chasing something nobody would eat.
explanation.walkthrough: Oscar Wilde called the chase 'the unspeakable in full pursuit of the uneatable'.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilde's famous line describes riding after an animal that no one eats, so this is an allusive definition.

clue.text: Pompous speech minister has dashed through

indicators.note: the word for dashed goes through the minister, sitting inside his name

parts.note: William Hague was Foreign Secretary
to have dashed is to have run, ran

explanation.surface: A minister rushing through a bombastic speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A harangue is a long, loud, ranting address, a forceful and often pompous lecture.

clue.text: House not entirely accepting animal sport

indicators.note: accepting means the shortened word takes the animal inside
not entirely means the last letter is removed

parts.note: house is another name for the game of bingo, called in British halls
an ox is a farm animal

explanation.surface: A house that partly admits animal fighting as a sport.
explanation.walkthrough: House, or housey-housey, is an old British name for bingo, the numbers game.
explanation.definitionFit: Fighting with fists in a ring is a combat sport.

clue.text: See 1 across
It's unacceptable, however you look at it

indicators.note: looked at from either direction the letters read the same

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Something is wrong whichever way you consider it.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying a thing is beyond the pale or not acceptable is the British idiom used here.

clue.text: Minister managed to overlook a rule

parts.note: Michael Gove was Education Secretary

indicators.note: to overlook something is to leave it out, so the a is dropped

parts.note: to have managed something is to have run it, ran

explanation.surface: A minister who managed to ignore a regulation.
explanation.definitionFit: To rule a country is to govern it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Awful slut I was, in some cases

indicators.note: awful means terrible, so the letters are badly rearranged

explanation.surface: A confession of past bad behaviour that came up in court.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal actions brought in court are called cases, so this is a plain synonym.

clue.text: Biblical character in Joshua sent reeling

indicators.note: reeling means turning back, so the found letters are read backwards
in says the letters sit inside the words Joshua sent

explanation.surface: Joshua, the Old Testament figure, being sent staggering.
explanation.definitionFit: Esau was the elder son of Isaac in Genesis, who sold his birthright to Jacob.

clue.text: Tell twice one's alone

parts.note: to sing is to tell, to inform on someone
to let on is to tell, to reveal a secret

explanation.surface: Telling something twice because you are by yourself.
explanation.definitionFit: A singleton is a person on their own, unattached, so it describes someone alone.
